en_title: TWO FACTORS THAT GIVE YOUR BUSINESS SALES CONSISTENCY.
en_excerpt: Selling more is not the secret to a lasting business. How you welcome customers and the experience you create around them is what builds loyalty.
en_meta_description: How welcoming customers and a great buying experience build loyalty and consistent sales for your small business.
en_content:
By Sonia Campos, Master's in Information Science and Specialist in Business Intelligence.

instagram: https://www.instagram.com/soninhafields/

In an increasingly competitive market, many entrepreneurs believe that the secret to success lies simply in selling more. However, the sustainability of a business depends on factors far deeper than a single commercial transaction. Among them, two stand out for their ability to generate loyalty, referrals and continuous growth: how you welcome the customer and the buying experience.

The first contact is decisive. Even before assessing prices or terms, the customer assesses people. Friendliness, courtesy, lightness, good humour and genuine attention create an emotional connection that opens the door to trust. Showing mastery of the product or service conveys confidence, but knowing how to listen matters just as much. Many entrepreneurs make the mistake of presenting their solutions before understanding the customer's real needs.

When we ask questions, listen attentively and seek to understand the challenges of the person in front of us, we can offer a more suitable, personalised solution. People like buying from those who convey positive energy, credibility and a genuine interest in helping them.

Excellent customer service may not generate an immediate sale, but it is a guaranteed future sale!

The second factor is the buying experience. The relationship with the customer does not end when the sale is closed. On the contrary, that is the moment when loyalty starts to be built. Every detail matters: communication, customer service, delivery, follow-up and how the customer feels throughout the whole journey.

Businesses that positively surprise their customers create a lasting memory. Delivering more than you promised does not necessarily mean spending more, but rather adding value through attention, care and excellence in the details. A small gesture can turn a satisfied customer into a true promoter of your brand.

In the end, consistent businesses are built by people who understand that selling is not just offering a product or a service, but creating relationships and memorable experiences. Customers may forget what they bought, but they rarely forget how they were treated.

That is what sets a simple sale apart from a sustainable business!

Sonia Campos

Entrepreneur and Master in Market Intelligence.
